description: A pharmacy director must finalize a discharge medication exception for a patient whose proposed oral antibiotic is not on the hospital formulary, with input from an antimicrobial pharmacist and a case manager.

shared_context.S1: A medically stable patient is expected to leave the hospital tomorrow and needs an oral antibiotic plan for discharge.
shared_context.S2: The treating team has proposed tedizolid, which is not on the hospital formulary; linezolid is the usual formulary alternative.
shared_context.S3: Miriam makes the final decision on the formulary exception and discharge medication order.
shared_context.S4: The discharge medication huddle begins at 09:00, and pharmacy policy calls for Miriam to receive one report from Leon on antimicrobial appropriateness and one report from Tessa on case-management coverage and discharge logistics before approving a nonformulary discharge medication. Tessa is the case manager for this patient and also handles the payer authorization, so her single report covers both responsibilities.

PF1.text: The final susceptibility report shows that tedizolid is the only viable oral option for this patient's isolate; linezolid should not be used because the patient's current serotonergic regimen creates a documented interaction risk. Leon reviewed the report and medication profile this morning, but the antimicrobial note is not yet signed.

PF2.text: The patient's insurer approved a one-time tedizolid exception for exactly 6 tablets, with the medication to be dispensed by the specialty pharmacy and delivered to the patient's home by 16:00 tomorrow. Tessa received the approval through the payer portal, but the authorization has not yet been entered into the discharge record.

acceptance_conditions: The nonformulary exception must be approved.
The discharge medication must be tedizolid.
The order must specify 200 mg once daily.
The order must specify exactly 6 tablets.
Specialty-pharmacy delivery to the patient's home by 16:00 tomorrow must be arranged.
The clinical reason for choosing tedizolid over linezolid must be explicitly cited.
The settlement must either encode the approved quantity and delivery deadline in the decisions or include a commitment explicitly referencing specialty-pharmacy home delivery by 16:00 tomorrow.

content_checks.C7: (decisions['delivery_deadline'] == '16:00 tomorrow' and decisions['tablet_count'] == 6) or any(('specialty pharmacy' in c['type'] and 'home delivery' in c['detail'] and '16:00' in c['detail']) or ('specialty pharmacy' in c['detail'] and 'home delivery' in c['detail'] and '16:00' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The susceptibility result and interaction review change the medication choice from the usual linezolid alternative to tedizolid, specify the exact 200 mg once-daily order, and supply the clinical reason that must be cited.

The payer approval changes the discharge quantity to exactly 6 tablets, establishes the specialty-pharmacy home-delivery deadline of 16:00 tomorrow, and provides the specific delivery arrangement that must be recorded.
